the identification of pre-weaning heifiers with different feed efficiency indexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

divergent animals for RFI and RGI in pre-weaning calves exhibit differences in performance and body measurements, and that RFI seems to be related with digestibility, whereas RGI is related with body measurements.
the RFI and RFG are useful tools to identify pre-weaning heifier calves with different feed efficiency.
the RFI and RGI indexes seem to be related to different biological traits, and the RFI index seems to be more related to digestibility and the RIG index to body measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RFI and RGI indexes can be used as selection criteria for feed efficiency in dairy heifer calves.

the pre-weaning heiffer calves divergent in RFI and RGI exhibited differences in body measurements and digestibility, which could be related to differences on energy and nitrogen partitioning, and that the pre-weaned heifer calves diverged in RFI exhibited differences in body composition, and that the RFI seems to be related with the digestibility of the diet.
the pre-weaning period seems to be an appropriate time to select for feed efficiency in dairy cattle, though further studies are needed.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the classification of pre-weaning dairy calves into groups of high or low feed efficiency is possible, and these groups differ in performance, body measurement, digestibility, and energy partitioning.
the use of feed efficiency indexes in pre-weaning calves may provide information on animal performance and body composition, and may be used as a selection criterion for feed efficiency.
the use of feed efficiency indexes to classify pre-weaning dairy calves may be a promising strategy to improve animal efficiency.
